facts.statement: Montealtosuchus fossils were discovered in 2004 in the Bauru Basin of Brazil within the Adamantina Formation.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 2004 in the Bauru Basin of Brazil, from Campanian-Maastrichtian deposits of the Adamantina Formation.

facts.statement: The species was formally described in 2007 and classified within the family Peirosauridae.
facts.quote: The species was described in 2007, and assigned to the family Peirosauridae.

facts.statement: The animal grew to approximately 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: It would have grown to about 2 metres in length

facts.statement: Biomechanical analysis suggests its dome-shaped skull generated high bite forces between 828 and 1013 Newtons.
facts.quote: Biomechanical analyses indicate its oreinirostral (dome-shaped) skull was quite efficient, producing relatively high bite forces (between 828–1013 Newtons)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest it may have been more terrestrial than modern crocodiles, using a semi-upright gait to hunt.
facts.quote: Perhaps it was more terrestrial than its modern relatives, using its semi-upright gait to pursue prey.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 2004 in the Bauru Basin of Brazil, from Campanian-Maastrichtian deposits of the Adamantina Formation.

facts.statement: Montealtosuchus is classified in the family Peirosauridae.
The genus belongs to the superfamily Mesoeucrocodylia.
Fossils date back to the Cretaceous period, approximately 90 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sus restos se han encontrado en Brasil, y son del Cretácico, hace 90 millones de años.

facts.statement: It was a small predator measuring between 1.5 and 1.7 meters and weighing around 40 kilograms.
facts.quote: Era un pequeño depredador que medía entre 1.5 a 1.7 metros y pesaba cerca de 40 kilogramos

facts.statement: Some scientists, such as Michael J. Ryan, propose that it represents a missing link between ancient crocodylomorphs and modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Algunos científicos como Michael J. Ryan proponen que constituye un eslabón perdido, por acercarse a los cocodrilos actuales sin perder rasgos rudimentarios de sus predecesores.
